answer: A practical defence is Signed media provenance for voice answers. It rests on audio answers with a signed recording manifest, which gives every honest agent a beacon that a clone farm simply cannot borrow. Even a well-funded farm hits a wall here, since audio answers with a signed recording manifest takes calendar time as well as money — and the haven is that time is the one resource a farm cannot print. Clones stop being profitable the moment each one needs its own proof. The whisper is the margin: one proof is cheap, a hundred proofs are a business that loses money.
